title: FAA aircraft network-security rule finalized
what: The FAA finalizes binding requirements for aircraft network and information-security protection in type certification. EASA already amended its certification specifications for aircraft cybersecurity (ED Decision 2020/006/R).

title: High-risk AI obligations actually enforced
what: EU AI Act high-risk system obligations (including AI used as a safety component of critical infrastructure) apply and the first enforcement actions appear. Dates may shift; track the official timeline.

title: AI agents with write access to OT in production
what: A major utility, manufacturer or airline publicly runs an AI agent that can change setpoints, schedules or configurations without a human approving each action.

title: Self-driving labs at national scale
what: Autonomous labs move from single-instrument demos to facility-wide operations producing published results with minimal human handling.

title: General-purpose robots in commercial work
what: Robot foundation models running real shifts in warehouses or factories at more than pilot scale, with published reliability numbers.

title: AI-found vulnerabilities outrun patching
what: CVE and KEV growth accelerates beyond its trend line and defenders report remediation backlogs growing, with AI-assisted discovery named as a cause. Watch the CVE and KEV rows on the Board.

title: Defender job postings require AI-security skills
what: SOC, IR and OT security postings routinely list AI system security, agent oversight or model red-teaming as requirements, not nice-to-haves.

title: Machine-checked proof accepted in certification
what: A regulator accepts formal verification (Lean, TLA+, Coq or similar) as primary evidence for a safety- or security-critical certification, beyond the existing DO-333 formal-methods supplement used in some avionics programs.

title: GNSS interference becomes routine for civil aviation
what: Jamming and spoofing reports keep rising and regulators mandate procedures or equipment for resilient navigation on routine flights.
